classification.difficultyReason: Subtract the remaining volume from the full cylinder volume, then use the square-prism volume to find its side length.

content.prompt: A solid cylinder has a shaft with a square cross-section through it, as shown in the diagram below. The volume of the solid is $(500\pi-80)\text{ cm}^3$. Calculate the length of a side of the square cross-section.

spec.description: Upright cylinder with a square shaft extending through its full height. The top square opening is solid; shaft edges and its lower square are dashed. The lower circular boundary has a dashed rear half and solid front half. External dimensions show height and diameter.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder diameter 10 cm and height 20 cm; an unknown square cross-section is removed through the full height.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied dimensions appear; the shaft side length is not labelled.

sizing.exceptionReason: Reviewed narrow/tall source solid: retain proportional geometry, all dimensions and native 10 pt labels. Height above the ordinary 40 mm review trigger may be necessary for distinguishable marks; working space is unchanged.

answer.worked:
The cylinder has radius $10\div2=5\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cylinder}}&=\pi\times5^2\times20\\V_{\text{cylinder}}&=500\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{shaft}}&=500\pi-(500\pi-80)\\V_{\text{shaft}}&=80\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

Let $s$ cm be the side length of the square cross-section. The shaft is a square prism of height $20\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}20s^2&=80\\s^2&=4\\s&=2\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
